{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
df['revenue_clean'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Filter out QA test orders (revenue = 999999.99)
qa_mask = df['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99

# Filter out refunded orders
refunded_mask = df['status'] == 'refunded'

# Apply filters: keep only completed orders and non-QA orders
filtered_df = df[~qa_mask & ~refunded_mask]

# Check the number of rows
print(f"Number of rows after filtering: {filtered_df.shape[0]}")

# Compute conversion rate for each channel and customer_segment
segment_channel_conv = filtered_df.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment'])['converted'].mean().unstack(level='channel')

# Extract conversion rates
email_conv_by_segment = segment_channel_conv['email']
paid_search_conv_by_segment = segment_channel_conv['paid_search']

# Compute difference in conversion rates within each segment
differences_by_segment = email_conv_by_segment - paid_search_conv_by_segment

# Compute the weight for each segment: proportion of orders in the email channel
email_segment_counts = filtered_df[filtered_df['channel'] == 'email']['customer_segment'].value_counts()
total_email = email_segment_counts.sum()
weights = email_segment_counts / total_email

# Compute the weighted average of the segment-specific differences
weighted_difference = (differences_by_segment * weights).sum()

# Print results
print(f"Conversion rates by segment:")
print(segment_channel_conv)
print(f"Segment-specific differences (email - paid_search):\n{differences_by_segment}")
print(f"Weights (based on email channel distribution):\n{weights}")
print(f"Weighted average difference (adjusted for confounding): {weighted_difference}")"}
